hep-ex.title: Measurements of isolated photon pair production in association with jets in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 8 TeV with the ATLAS detector
hep-ex.author: ATLAS Collaboration
hep-ex.abstract: Measurements of integrated and differential production cross section of two isolated photons in events with and without associated hadronic jets based on the 2012 dataset of 20.3 fb$^{-1}$ integrated luminosity of proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=8$ TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment are presented. The measurements consider photons with pseudorapidities of $|\eta^{\gamma}|<1.37$ or $1.56<|\eta^{\gamma}|<2.37$ and transverse energy of $E_{T}^{\gamma}>22$ GeV. Jets are required to have $p_{T}^{j}>25$ GeV for $|\eta^{j}|<2.4$ and $p_{T}^{j}>50$ GeV for $2.4<|\eta^{j}|<4.4$. Events are classified into categories based on the number of jets and integrated fiducial cross sections of diphoton production in association with inclusive and exclusive number of jets are presented. Fiducial cross sections, differential in sixteen diphoton, jet, dijet and photon-jet observables, are presented and compared with leading-order Sherpa 1.4.1 predictions in all jet categories, fixed-order next-to-leading-order GoSam and BlackHat calculations in selected categories, and NLO-matched predictions from Sherpa 2.2.14 in all categories. Overall, the NLO predictions provide a reasonable description of the data, with significant discrepancies observed for increasing jet multiplicity, particularly for angular variables, attributable to the absence of higher-order terms in the calculations. The Sherpa 2.2.14 NLO-matched predictions provide the best overall description of the data across all jet categories and observables.

hep-ex.title: Operational Challenges in Efficient and Sustainable Operation of the Event Processing Nodes GPU Farm at the ALICE Experiment
hep-ex.author: Federico Ronchetti, Giada Erba
hep-ex.abstract: ALICE's Event Processing Nodes (EPN) farm is CERN's largest GPU computing facility by capacity, comprising 350 GPU-based nodes and 2800 GPUs delivering approximately a total of 48\,PFLOP/s. It has successfully enabled real-time processing of heavy-ion collisions at 50\,kHz during LHC Run~3. The facility was designed for sustainability, extended hardware lifetime, and reduced operational overhead. High availability is supported by a robust technical architecture and well-defined operational practices, ensuring reliable and continuous operation throughout data taking.

hep-ex.title: Photon-Counting Readout via Electro-Optic Microwave-to-Optical Transduction for Axion Haloscopes
hep-ex.author: Jing Wu, Raphael Cervantes, Doga Murat Kurkcuoglu, Zheshen Zhang, Silvia Zorzetti
hep-ex.abstract: Axion dark matter searches require highly sensitive detection schemes with high scan rate to efficiently explore the parameter space. Building upon the conventional Sikivie haloscope, where axions convert into microwave photons inside a magnetic-field-immersed resonant cavity, we present a photon-counting scheme based on an electro-optic microwave-to-optical transducer. Through a comprehensive theoretical model under realistic experimental constraints, we find that the optimal operating regime employs an overcoupled microwave cavity, trading peak transduction efficiency for reduced transducer noise. Furthermore, combining parameters already demonstrated in existing devices, in a device with optimized extrinsic coupling rates, would yield a scan-rate enhancement of 5-10 relative to quantum-limited homodyne detection. Improvements in quality factors, coupling rates, and thermal management push this enhancement beyond 50. While our quantitative model is benchmarked at 9 GHz, the scheme adapts well to haloscopes across the 5-12 GHz range, where shrinking cavity volumes severely degrade the achievable scan rate. These results demonstrate the potential of electro-optical photon detection as a high-speed detection technique for axion dark matter searches.

hep-ex.title: The Search for the Top Quark
hep-ex.author: Paul D. Grannis
hep-ex.abstract: The discovery of the top quark in 1995 completed the roster of the matter particles, quarks and leptons, expected in the Standard Model and in many of its suggested extensions. However, the top quark does not conform to the pattern set by its sister quarks and has come to be a critical component of the ongoing searches for physics beyond the prevailing paradigm. (Prepared for the Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, Nov. 2025.)

hep-ex.title: Top Spin and CP from Equivariant Transformers
hep-ex.author: Henning Bahl, Marco Menen, Antoine Petitjean, Tilman Plehn
hep-ex.abstract: Measurements of spin correlations and CP are an exciting and challenging part of the precision-LHC program. We first show how L-GATr-slim, as a Lorentz-equivariant transformer, significantly boosts the spin analyzing power for hadronic top quarks. We then show how adding a pseudoscalar channel to its architecture allows us to learn and interpret optimal observables and their CP properties. We demonstrate this for WBF-Higgs production at parton level and top pair production including detector effects.

hep-ex.title: Indirect probes of heavy neutral leptons through the dipole portal at FCC-ee
hep-ex.author: Natascia Vignaroli
hep-ex.abstract: We study indirect probes of the gauge-invariant dipole portal of Majorana heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at FCC-ee. Virtual HNLs modify electroweak gauge-boson propagation and lepton couplings through loops with two dipole interactions. We calculate the resulting finite matching corrections and their effects on $Z$-pole observables. For real, flavour-aligned couplings, the local response is specified by four combinations of coupling shifts. Independent local ultraviolet interactions can reproduce all four, making the dipole interpretation dependent on assumptions about those interactions. With improved Standard Model predictions, FCC-ee can probe equal, same-sign hypercharge and weak dipole coefficients as small as $0.14\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$ at an HNL mass of 1 TeV. This projection assumes dipole dominance, with independent ultraviolet coefficients set to zero at twice the HNL mass. We quantify how additional ultraviolet contributions can weaken or strengthen the sensitivity. At 1 TeV, the projected reach is competitive with HL-LHC same-sign dilepton searches for Majorana HNLs, while larger masses allow smaller dipole coefficients to be probed within the effective theory's domain of validity. Radiative Higgs decays offer a modest further improvement. The FeynRules, FeynArts and UFO models used in this analysis are publicly available at \href{this https URL}{doi:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667622}.

hep-ex.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
hep-ex.author: A. Capelo-Astudillo, T. Aguilar, M. Conde-Correa, A. Duenas-Vidal, P. G. Ortega, J. Segovia
hep-ex.abstract: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

hep-ex.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
hep-ex.author: Joe Wiedemann, Roman Kolevatov, Jianyang Fu, Joelle-Marie Begin, Nate Otto, Felix St-Amour, Lyman Page, Henry LeDuc, Peter Day, Saptarshi Chaudhuri
hep-ex.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.

hep-ex.title: Born spreading with consistent shower starting scales in MC@NLO and FxFx merging
hep-ex.author: Rikkert Frederix, Paolo Torrielli
hep-ex.abstract: Negative weights are a major cost in NLO event generation matched to parton showers at the LHC, as they increase the number of events needed for a given statistical precision. Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative-weight $\mathbb S$ events in MC@NLO by redistributing the Born contribution over the radiation variables. It introduces no bias only if everything that is passed to the parton shower together with $\mathbb S$ events depends on Born-level quantities alone. We show that the same condition is needed for the MC counterterms to reproduce the first shower emission, independently of how the radiation phase space is integrated. In MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, the $\mathbb S$-event starting scales did not fully satisfy this condition, which so far prevented the public release of Born spreading. We present a new and consistent construction of the starting scales for ordinary MC@NLO, FxFx merging and MC@NLO-$\Delta$, with which Born spreading is now publicly available, including for merged samples. We also study modified formulations of the MC counterterms, and FxFx-merged $W$+jets production with up to two jets at NLO, for which Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative weights after merging without affecting the predictions, and the event samples are generated six times faster than with the former implementation.

hep-ex.title: CMS ECAL Phase-2 upgrade: characterisation and stability analysis of a three-stage low-voltage power-conversion system
hep-ex.author: Liv Anke Richter, Günther Dissertori, Werner Lustermann, Krzysztof Stachon
hep-ex.abstract: As part of the High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider, the front-end electronics of the Compact Muon Solenoid electromagnetic calorimeter barrel are being replaced. A three-stage low-voltage power-conversion system supplies the upgraded electronics. As the cascade dynamics require characterisation to ensure stable operation, interactions between the three converter stages are assessed at their two interfaces using the Nyquist criterion. A validated shunt-injection setup using a Bode 100 frequency-response analyser provides in-situ impedance measurements under load to assess the accuracy of the averaged converter models. Results show that both interfaces are stable over the evaluated configurations, with modelled minimum distances to the critical point of 0.76 and 0.79, respectively. A turn-on study identifies capacitor charging at Stage 3 as the main cause of inrush currents triggering Stage 2 overcurrent protection. Two Stage 3 board variants stagger converter enables within and between boards, keeping the measured two-tower current below 5 A, within the 8.0 A protection threshold.

hep-ex.title: Cross-Moment Consistency and the Fifth Adler Coefficient in Hadronic Tau Decays
hep-ex.author: Gauhar Abbas, Debabina Biswas, Pratham Dadhich, Vartika Singh
hep-ex.abstract: The unknown coefficient $c_{5,1}$ controls the first omitted fifth-order term in fixed-order analyses of inclusive hadronic $\tau$ decays. We determine what the four known Adler coefficients can actually test. For any normalized polynomial weight, the fixed-order Adler-to-moment map is triangular with unit diagonal. Hence one common Adler-coefficient error reaches every moment with the same absolute size, and a multi-weight relative test reduces to one absolute tolerance. For three representative weights, a ten-percent test resolves $c_{5,1}$ only to about $\pm24$; the closest contour-improved test is weaker by more than an order of magnitude. Moreover, any continuation that preserves the observed sign of the direct Padé/Shanks defects gives $c_{5,1}\geq378.03$, so values near $280$ require additional structure. A calibration-and-falsification protocol applied to a simplified Beneke--Jamin-type pure-power ansatz gives the conditional estimate $c_{5,1}=248\pm30\,(\mathrm{struct})\pm74\,(\mathrm{method})=248\pm80$. At the physical order its central value coincides algebraically with the exact four-parameter fit; the protocol adds a falsifiable admissibility test and a method uncertainty, not new coefficient information. We also clarify that the often-quoted Beneke--Jamin value $283$ is a linear extrapolation of total-width FOPT te

hep-ex.title: Chromatic Calorimetry -- A Novel Approach to Validate Energy Resolution and Particle Discrimination
hep-ex.author: Devanshi Arora
hep-ex.abstract: Chromatic calorimetry (CCAL) analyses particle detection by utilizing scintillators with distinct emission wavelengths to measure the longitudinal energy deposition of particle showers in high-energy physics, improving particle identification (PID) and energy resolution. By stacking scintillators in order of decreasing emission wavelength, CCAL enables layer-specific energy measurements, analyzed via amplitude fractions ($f_i = A_i / \sum_j A_j$) and center of gravity ($\langle z_{\text{cog}} \rangle = \sum_i z_i E_i / \sum_i E_i$). This thesis presents results from two CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) experiments conducted in 2023 and 2024, complemented by GEANT4 simulations of a quantum dot (QD)-based CCAL design, to validate its potential for future colliders such as the Future Circular Collider (FCC).

hep-ex.title: Deep Sets and event-level maximum-likelihood estimation for fast pile-up jet rejection at the ATLAS High Level Trigger
hep-ex.author: Mohammed Aboelela
hep-ex.abstract: Multiple proton-proton interactions occur in the same bunch crossing at the LHC ("pile-up"), with the mean number of interactions per bunch crossing reaching up to about 60 in Run 3 and up to about 200 at the High-Luminosity LHC. As a direct consequence, hadronic activity within each bunch crossing increases, making it more difficult to identify collisions of interest pertaining to multijet final states. This work introduces DIPz, an uncertainty-aware Deep Sets-based machine-learning model that estimates each jet's origin along the beam axis as a Gaussian likelihood using the set of charged-particle tracks matched to the jet. Next, the DIPz predictions for each jet are combined into a likelihood-based event-level discriminant, which is optimised to select events compatible with a single collision producing a given jet multiplicity. This combined approach provides a robust and computationally efficient method for pile-up rejection in multijet final states, applicable to real-time event selections at the ATLAS High Level Trigger (HLT). Deployed online during Run 3 data taking, this approach reduces background rates by more than a factor of two, and decreases CPU consumption by approximately one third relative to the baseline data-taking configuration. It provides an early, flavour-agnostic pile-up jet rejection layer at the HLT preselection stage, introducing a previously unavailable handle for high-multiplicity jet signatures targeted by ATLAS.

hep-ex.title: Machine-learned particle flow as a foundation model for collider physics
hep-ex.author: Farouk Mokhtar, Joosep Pata, Michael Kagan, Javier Duarte
hep-ex.abstract: The workflow from particle collision to physics analysis passes through a series of reconstruction steps that are traditionally modular and disconnected, with no shared representation linking low-level detector data to high-level analysis tasks. We show that casting event reconstruction as a machine learning problem naturally produces such a shared representation. We repurpose a machine learning model trained for particle-flow reconstruction (MLPF) to perform three distinct analysis tasks: jet flavor identification, jet energy regression, and missing momentum regression. By appending the per-particle latent representations learned during reconstruction as additional input features, we substantially improve over baselines that use conventional particle-level features alone. We further demonstrate that a single linear layer trained using only the latent representations achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art baseline architectures, and outperforms the baseline for missing momentum regression with approximately 35 times fewer parameters. These results demonstrate that the latent representations learned during reconstruction encode essential physics information needed for downstream analysis, establishing MLPF as a foundation model and offering a concrete step toward an end-to-end pipeline from detector data to physics analysis.

Bhattacharya, M.S. Bieker, N.V. Biesuz, A. Biolchini, M. Birch, F.C.R. Bishop, A. Bitadze, A. Bizzeti, T. Blake, F. Blanc
hep-ex.abstract: A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $0.228~\mathrm{nb}^{-1}$ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV. This is the first search for axion-like particles produced exclusively by two photons ($\gamma\gamma\to a\to\gamma\gamma$) in the forward direction. It extends sensitivity to previously unexplored regions of the parameter space, probing axion-like particle masses and couplings down to 3.0 GeV and $3.2\times10^{-4}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, respectively. This result provides the most stringent limits to date on the production of axion-like particles from exclusive photon-photon fusion processes with masses between 3 and 5 GeV.

hep-ex.title: Hard X-ray/Soft gamma-ray Laue Lenses for High Energy Astrophysics
hep-ex.author: Filippo Frontera
hep-ex.abstract: The study of the celestial phenomena in the hard X-ray/soft gamma-ray band(20 keV--1 MeV) is very intriguing but also very difficult to be performed with the needed sensitivity. In this review I will discuss the astrophysical importance of the soft gamma-ray astronomy, its difficulties to solve its issues with the current instrumentation, and a possible solution achievable using focusing Laue lens. Concerning these instruments, I will discuss their functioning principle, how to achieve a high reflection efficiency, their imaging properties, the current feasibility studies, the technological developments and observation prospects.

hep-ex.title: EFT Validity and Truncation Uncertainty from few Nuisance Parameters
hep-ex.author: Benoît Assi, Adam Martin, William Shepherd
hep-ex.abstract: An observable in an Effective Field Theory (EFT) is an expansion in a set of small parameters, no different than any other perturbation series. Truncating such a series expansion leaves the leading dropped term as the dominant source of error, and that term itself contains a calculable portion. We explore the partial calculation of this next-order error, available at dim-6$^2$ in SMEFT with no additional tools needed to simulate it, and explore how to efficiently use that partial calculation to model the next-order uncertainty in full using a minimal number of nuisance parameters. This estimate of the uncertainty of the EFT signal rate naturally imposes EFT validity by ensuring that bounds are driven by kinematic regions where truncation uncertainties are parametrically smaller than the signal. We incorporate the calculable dim-6$^2$ piece into the signal and cover the remaining higher-dimension uncertainty with a small set of nuisance parameters derived from a scan over Wilson-coefficient values. Our algorithm to determine the relevant nuisance parameters and distributions is automation-friendly and applies to arbitrary truncation choices. We then provide multiple examples of its implementation in high-energy collider processes focused on SMEFT truncated at $\mathcal{O}(\Lambda^{-2})$, where the dim-6$^2$ piece is used to estimate the full $\mathcal O(\Lambda^{-4})$ dependence. In the examples considered here the reduction of nuisance parameters is appreciable, generically reducing the nuisance parameter count by an order of magnitude compared to naive estimates.

hep-ex.title: Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering at low and high energies
hep-ex.author: Yoshitaka Hatta, Víctor Martínez-Fernández
hep-ex.abstract: We study spin-spin entanglement in the final state photon-nucleon system in Compton scattering, both at low energy below the pion threshold and at high energy in perturbative QCD to next-to-leading order. We first establish a no-go theorem showing that, for any spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ target, entanglement cannot be generated in unpolarized Compton scattering if the scattering amplitudes are real. We then consider polarized Compton scattering off the electron, the proton and the neutron. At low energy, we uncover a rich variety of maximally entangled Bell states and their unitary equivalents realized across different regions of the kinematic plane. Interestingly, the proton and neutron targets exhibit distinct patterns of entanglement. In the neutron case, the electric and magnetic polarizabilities dramatically influence the pattern and even the existence of entanglement. This suggests that entanglement can serve as a novel tool for investigating the detailed electromagnetic properties of the nucleons.

hep-ex.title: Inelastic Dark Matter and High-Energy Recoil Signatures in LZ
hep-ex.author: Zi-Tong Fan, Hong-Jian He, Yu-Chen Wang, Yue Zhao
hep-ex.abstract: We study the inelastic dark matter (iDM) that consists of two-component dark matter particles $(\chi_1,\chi_2)$ and serves as a minimal extension beyond the commonly used one-component DM models. A distinctive feature of such iDM scattering with the target nuclei is to favorably produce signals at high nuclear recoil (NR) energy region in both exothermic and endothermic processes. In particular, for the exothermic dark matter scenario, the signal does not rely on the tail of the Boltzmann velocity distribution. As a result, the required DM-nucleus scattering cross section is significantly reduced, which in turn helps to substantially relax the stringent constraints imposed by IceCube neutrino searches. Using the inelastic DM-nucleus scattering, we naturally explain the newly reported event excess at high recoil energy with the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment.

hep-ex.title: ISR Reconstruction of Radiative $C=+1$ Charmonia as the Origin of the Belle--BESIII Line-Shape Puzzle
hep-ex.author: Cheng-Xi Liu, Tian-Le Gao, Cheng-Ping Shen, Xiang Liu
hep-ex.abstract: A longstanding disagreement persists between Belle and BESIII over the line shapes of $e^+e^-\to \Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$, $D_sD_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_sD_{s2}^{*}(2573)$ near 4.63 GeV. Belle observes enhancements through initial state radiation that are absent or much weaker at BESIII. We propose that the extra Belle yield arises from radiative production of a $C=+1$ charmonium. Luminosity normalization increases this contribution to the extracted cross sections, so tens of fb can explain the enhancements. Belle II can test this mechanism through full reconstruction and searches for missing charmonia in open charm modes.

hep-ex.title: "Inevitable" nonstrange tetraquark states and $ρρ$ interaction
hep-ex.author: Yanyue Pan, Yuying Hao, Shirui Zhao, Hongxia Huang, Jialun Ping
hep-ex.abstract: Investigation of the interaction between two $\rho$ mesons with $IJ = 00,~02,~11,~20$ and $22$ is conducted systematically in the framework of the quark delocalization color screening model. The results show that there is a strong attractive potential between two $\rho$ mesons, which makes it easier for these two mesons to form bound states. The binding energies vary from a few MeV to over a hundred MeV. Moreover, the results of intercluster distances favor a molecular interpretation of these states. The interaction analysis reveals that the $\rho\rho$ and $\Delta\Delta$ interactions share certain similarities. Drawing inspiration from the $d^*$ dibaryon prediction and from decay-property analyses, we predict that the $\rho\rho$ with $IJ=02$ and $22$ are the most promising candidates of the ``inevitable'' nonstrange tetraquark states, which deserves experimental search.

hep-ex.title: Resolving the Two-Fold Ambiguity in Tau Momentum Reconstruction via a Self-Consistent Weighting Method
hep-ex.author: Rong-Gang Ping
hep-ex.abstract: The reconstruction of $\tau$ lepton momenta in $e^{+}e^{-} \to \tau^{+}\tau^{-}$ processes suffers from a two-fold kinematic ambiguity due to undetected neutrinos. We show that the common practice of retaining both solutions with equal weight systematically biases the extracted angular coefficients: the bias grows with the size of the $\cos^{2}\theta$ modulation of the production distribution $f(\cos\theta)$, but remains resolvable even in the nearly uniform QED limit at the $\psi(2S)$ threshold. We propose a self-consistent weighting method based on a fixed-point theorem: assigning normalized weights $w_{i} = f(\cos\theta_{i})/[f(\cos\theta_{1})+f(\cos\theta_{2})]$ yields a weighted distribution $h(x) = f(x)[1+\varepsilon(x)]$ with $\varepsilon(x) \ll 1$ under a detailed balance condition. Monte Carlo simulations at $\sqrt{s}=3.686$~GeV and $4.8$~GeV show that the fixed-point iteration converges to the true angular coefficient $\alpha$ within statistical uncertainty, providing a robust framework for angular analysis without event-by-event ambiguity resolution.

hep-ph.title: Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
hep-ph.author: S.Bondarenko, M.Ouchen, A.Prygarin
hep-ph.abstract: Parton multiplicity entropy, proposed by Kharzeev and Levin as entanglement between the region probed in deep inelastic scattering and the proton's remainder, was compared with hadron multiplicity data. It is computed from parton densities, which do not fix the partons' quantum state. We show that a one-parton density matrix from Lipatov's wave functions determines two entropies for resolved modes with finite mean number and entropy. Its trace is the mean parton number, and normalization gives a sampled parton's entropy. A compatible thermal state, if it exists, maximizes entropy at fixed one-parton matrix. This maximum equals the actual entropy only for that thermal state and measures entanglement only for a specified subsystem of a pure state. The geometric multiplicity entropy follows if all emitted partons share one mode. An entropy computed from densities becomes such a maximum, an upper bound on the actual entropy, only for specified resolved modes. We also show that the state averaged over unrecorded emissions, assumed incoherent across scales, obeys probability-preserving Lindblad evolution on finitely many regulated modes with the resolution scale if emission and no-emission terms match. The occupations reproduce leading-order DGLAP, with virtual terms, at leading logarithmic accuracy as the cutoffs on momentum fractions are removed. The reduction holds for strongly ordered transverse momenta in light-cone gauge and dilute occupations, including those of newly resolved modes. Approximating momentum and helicity modes by independent thermal populations closes the occupation equation and gives this bound's evolution, with Bose and Pauli factors from the operator algebra. We propose testing this approximation at HERA or the LHC. The test compares the mode number inferred from normalized hadron factorial moments in a rapidity window with the window's transverse mode count.

hep-ph.title: Meson spectra in a screened relativized quark model
hep-ph.author: Zhe-Qi Huang, Lei Huang, Xiao-Lei Zhang, Xin-Lei Ge, Hao Chen, Cheng-Qun Pang
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we employed the modified Godfrey--Isgur model to systematically investigate the mass spectra of several light, heavy-light, and heavy-heavy meson systems. In this model, a screened potential is employed to phenomenologically account for modifications to the long-range confining interaction associated with unquenched effects. We performed a global refit of the relevant model parameters to a combined set of 90 adopted meson masses spanning all three sectors, ensuring a consistent parameter determination across the different meson systems. Using the resulting parameter set, we calculated the low-lying and highly excited spectra and the corresponding mixed states in different meson families, and compared our results with existing experimental data and other theoretical results. The assignment of several newly observed structures (such as $B_c^*$ and $D_{s1}(2933)$) have also been discussed based on their predicted masses. Overall, the model describes several main spectroscopic features across different flavors and provides mass predictions for highly excited states that have not yet been experimentally established.

hep-ph.title: Flavour Chains at the TeV Edge
hep-ph.author: Admir Greljo, Xavier Ponce Díaz, Lia Schöneweiß
hep-ph.abstract: We study chains of vector-like fermions that generate the Yukawa hierarchies as products of small mixings, with the Higgs coupled at a single link. Minimal Flavour Protection allows these flavour messengers to live at the TeV scale, while Higgs naturalness offers a reason to place them there: in cosmological solutions based on Higgs criticality, their large multiplicity lowers the critical point of the Higgs potential to the TeV scale. Crucially, the same Higgs interactions induce tree-level shifts in the $Z$ and $W$ couplings of light fermions. Existing LEP and SLD measurements already bound $M_F/|y_F|\gtrsim 3$ TeV, while a future Tera-$Z$ factory such as FCC-ee could probe up to $100$ TeV. It would test the parameter space most relevant to Higgs naturalness, reaching scenarios with Higgs-mass tuning at the level of $10^{-4}$ or worse in minimal realisations. Longer chains partially alleviate this tuning but do not eliminate it, making a Tera-$Z$ factory a decisive test of the framework.

hep-ph.title: Probing Heavier-Baryon Oscillations through Light-Baryon Mixing
hep-ph.author: Arnau Bas i Beneito, Svjetlana Fajfer, Alexey A. Petrov
hep-ph.abstract: Motivated by the existing direct limits on $\Xi_b^0$ and $\Xi_c^0$ oscillations, we investigate how Standard Model weak interactions connect baryon-number-violating mixing in heavy neutral baryons to the much more strongly constrained neutron-antineutron and $\Lambda-\bar\Lambda$ mixing. We focus on $\Xi_b^0$, $\Lambda_b^0$, $\Xi_c^0$, and $\Omega_c^0$ oscillations and derive indirect constraints on their mass-mixing parameters from existing limits on $n-\bar n$ oscillations and on $\Lambda-\bar\Lambda$ mixing, the latter inferred from dinucleon-decay searches. The weak baryon-to-baryon transition amplitudes are estimated by saturating the relevant hadronic correlators with low-lying intermediate baryons. The required weak vertices are modelled using semileptonic form factors from lattice QCD, quark models, and QCD sum rules. Since these form factors must be continued outside their physical semileptonic domains and the resulting loop integrals depend on a UV cutoff, our results are order-of-magnitude estimates subject to sizeable hadronic uncertainties. For a benchmark cutoff of $10~{\rm GeV}$, the indirect bounds on the $\Xi_b^0$ and $\Xi_c^0$ mixing parameters are roughly three and five orders of magnitude stronger than the direct LHCb and Belle limits, indicating that light-baryon $|\Delta B|=2$ searches can probe heavy-baryon oscillations far beyond present direct sensitivities.

hep-ph.title: Superconducting Qubits as Quantum Targets for Direct Particle Scattering
hep-ph.author: Doojin Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, Myeonghun Park
hep-ph.abstract: We introduce a novel approach to particle detection in which a superconducting qubit itself serves as the scattering target and a resolved transition between circuit eigenstates constitutes the observable final state. The scattering amplitude factorizes into the incident-particle current and a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition response of the qubit. This momentum dependence is essential in that the energy transfer is fixed by the microwave-scale level spacing, whereas a nonrelativistic incident particle can transfer a spatial momentum parametrically larger than that energy and thereby resolve the device geometry. For charge-dominated processes, we recast the response as an induced-offset-charge kernel obtained from an auxiliary electrostatic weighting potential, providing a practical route from circuit geometry to a differential scattering cross section. We illustrate the framework with an Xmon-style transmon and photon-mediated scattering of dark matter. The exceptionally small qubit transition threshold opens sensitivity to an eV-to-keV mass regime that is largely unexplored by existing direct-detection experiments.

hep-ph.title: Complete set of bounded-from-below conditions for the $A_4$-symmetric three-Higgs-doublet model
hep-ph.author: Luís Lavoura, André Milagre
hep-ph.abstract: We derive bounded-from-below necessary conditions for the scalar potential of an $A_4$-invariant three-Higgs-doublet model. The field Ansätze that we have used were devised with the help of Claude. Testing our set of conditions on $10^6$ random potentials, that in parallel we minimize by brute force using the Mathematica package StableWein, we find that the set seems to be necessary and sufficient for boundedness-from-below.

hep-ph.title: SMEFT Constraints on Top Electroweak Couplings and a Composite Higgs Interpretation
hep-ph.author: Leandro Da Rold, Juan Fernandez
hep-ph.abstract: Recent LHC measurements of $tWZ$, $t\bar t Z$ and single top production provide complementary probes of top quark electroweak interactions. We incorporate these measurements into a global Standard Model effective field theory analysis of 46 independent dimension-six Wilson coefficients at linear order. The updated fit remains compatible with the Standard Model at $95\%$ CL, and favors negative values of $C_{Hq}^{(-)}\equiv C_{Hq}^{(1)}-C_{Hq}^{(3)}$ and $C_{Ht}$, with central values suggestive of TeV scale new physics. We also present an effective composite Higgs model based on a two-site description that realizes this pattern of Wilson coefficients through partial compositeness. The model includes custodial symmetry and protection of the $Z\bar b_L b_L$ coupling. A fermion bitriplet generates the required left-handed shift, and an additional embedding of the right-handed top allows negative contributions to $C_{Ht}$ from both fermion and spin-one exchange. Scanning four right-handed top embeddings, we find parameter regions within the $68\%$ CL contour that are compatible with electroweak precision data, Higgs coupling measurements and applicable direct searches. The $T$ parameter limits the negative fermionic contribution to $C_{Ht}$, favoring a spin-one contribution of comparable or greater magnitude. Larger $SU(2)_R$ representations extend the reach toward negative $C_{Ht}$, and also enhance four-quark interactions that increase the four-top cross section, in the direction favored by current measurements. The mechanism connects the preferred top electroweak shifts to complementary tests through single production of quarks with electric charge $-4/3$, modified Higgs couplings and four-top production.

hep-ph.title: Indirect probes of heavy neutral leptons through the dipole portal at FCC-ee
hep-ph.author: Natascia Vignaroli
hep-ph.abstract: We study indirect probes of the gauge-invariant dipole portal of Majorana heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at FCC-ee. Virtual HNLs modify electroweak gauge-boson propagation and lepton couplings through loops with two dipole interactions. We calculate the resulting finite matching corrections and their effects on $Z$-pole observables. For real, flavour-aligned couplings, the local response is specified by four combinations of coupling shifts. Independent local ultraviolet interactions can reproduce all four, making the dipole interpretation dependent on assumptions about those interactions. With improved Standard Model predictions, FCC-ee can probe equal, same-sign hypercharge and weak dipole coefficients as small as $0.14\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$ at an HNL mass of 1 TeV. This projection assumes dipole dominance, with independent ultraviolet coefficients set to zero at twice the HNL mass. We quantify how additional ultraviolet contributions can weaken or strengthen the sensitivity. At 1 TeV, the projected reach is competitive with HL-LHC same-sign dilepton searches for Majorana HNLs, while larger masses allow smaller dipole coefficients to be probed within the effective theory's domain of validity. Radiative Higgs decays offer a modest further improvement. The FeynRules, FeynArts and UFO models used in this analysis are publicly available at \href{this https URL}{doi:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667622}.

hep-ph.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
hep-ph.author: A. Capelo-Astudillo, T. Aguilar, M. Conde-Correa, A. Duenas-Vidal, P. G. Ortega, J. Segovia
hep-ph.abstract: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

hep-ph.title: Probing CP Violation in the Complex 2HDMS with a 95 GeV Scalar at Future $e^+e^-$ Colliders
hep-ph.author: Jayita Lahiri, Cheng Li, Gudrid Moortgat-Pick
hep-ph.abstract: In this study, we investigate the prospects for probing CP violation in the complex singlet extension of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) at future electron-positron colliders. In extended scalar sectors, cancellations among different contributions to electric dipole moments (EDMs) can relax the stringent constraints on CP-violating phases, potentially bringing them in the current reach of collider experiments. We consider a scenario in which both the 125 GeV Higgs boson and the additional scalar associated with the reported 95 GeV excess are CP-mixed states. We probe the CP-violating phase of the 95 GeV scalar through its production via Higgsstrahlung and subsequent decay into a tau-lepton pair, using a CP-sensitive forward-backward asymmetry in hadronic and semileptonic tau-decay channels. We estimate the sensitivity at future lepton colliders, namely the ILC, FCC-ee, and CEPC, and investigate the impact of the Standard Model Drell-Yan background. We find that the hadronic channel offers greater sensitivity than the semileptonic channel. We also compare our results with existing constraints and future projections for CP violation in the 125 GeV Higgs sector and briefly discuss the implications for electroweak baryogenesis. Our results highlight the potential of future lepton colliders to probe CP violation in extended scalar sectors while remaining consistent with current EDM constraints.

hep-ph.title: The Cosmology of Hawking Axions
hep-ph.author: Abdelaziz Hussein, Gordan Krnjaic, Sarunas Verner
hep-ph.abstract: Since primordial black holes (PBH) are always non-relativistic, their cosmological energy fraction grows relative to that of radiation. Thus, for even a tiny initial PBH abundance, the universe generically enters an epoch of early matter domination, which ends when the PBH evaporate to restore the hot big bang. We consider the possibility that a PBH dominated era yields a population of boosted axion-like particles (ALPs) produced from Hawking evaporation. Eventually these ``Hawking axions" become non-relativistic and decay to photons, which can affect various cosmological and astrophysical observables. Here we place new constraints on these particles through their impact on big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, and X-ray observables. Furthermore, if Hawking axions remain relativistic through recombination, then depending on the progenitor PBH mass, they contribute $\Delta N_{\rm eff}\simeq0.05$-$0.11$, which may be observable with future CMB probes.

hep-ph.title: Hybrid Hadrons: Origins and Development
hep-ph.author: Eric S. Swanson
hep-ph.abstract: Hybrid hadrons are states in which the gluonic field of the strong force contributes to the structure of the hadron. The idea arose in several places at nearly the same time in the mid-1970s because the advent of quantum chromodynamics made it clear that the carriers of the strong force are dynamical degrees of freedom. This resulted in the cavity resonators of the MIT bag model, in the vibrating strings inherited from the dual resonance model, in the Budapest membrane bag, and in a constituent-gluon potential model. The idea was subsequently developed in the early 1980s into a phenomenology capable of predicting masses, quantum numbers, and decay signatures. This article traces that history from the primary literature, giving close attention to dates of submission and to who first proposed what, and supplements the written record with recollections of many of the principal participants. It closes by surveying the current state of experimental, theoretical, and lattice research.

hep-ph.title: Investigations on the low-lying $cccq\bar{q}$ resonances in a constituent quark model
hep-ph.author: Yue-Mei Yin, mao-jun Yan, Chun-Sheng An, Cheng-Rong Deng
hep-ph.abstract: In present work, mass spectrum of the low-lying $cccq\bar{q}$ pentaquarks states with $q\bar{q}=u\bar{u}$, $d\bar{d}$ and $s\bar{s}$, are investigated employing a constituent quark model, within which the spin-dependent hyperfine interactions are taken to be the instanton-induced interaction and the one-gluon-exchange interaction, respectively. The model parameters are fixed by fitting the mass spectrum of the relative $q\bar{q}$ and $qqq$ traditional hadrons. The numerical results show that energies for all the obtained states in the two employed models are higher than corresponding meson-baryon channels, consequently, we roughly estimate strong decays of these states using a simple quark rearrangement model, the corresponding partial width ratios for different decay channels are presented.

hep-ph.title: From lattice QCD thermodynamics to an effective quasiparticle description of gluonic matter at finite temperature
hep-ph.author: Cheng-Gang Guo, La-Yuan Peng, Zhen-Yan Lu, Marco Ruggieri, Shu-Peng Wang, Zhi-Jun Ma
hep-ph.abstract: We develop a lattice-constrained quasiparticle description of pure SU(3) Yang--Mills matter at finite temperature. The temperature-dependent effective gluon quasiparticle mass is determined from the lattice entropy density over $0.70\leq T/T_c\leq5$. It is interpreted as an effective thermal parameter encoding medium modifications of gluonic excitations, rather than as a physical gluon mass. With this mass fixed, we reconstruct the background contribution required for thermodynamic consistency, using a single pressure-normalization condition. The resulting pressure, energy density, entropy density, interaction measure, and squared speed of sound are then compared with available lattice results. Near $T_c$, the rapid variation of the effective mass is accompanied by a pronounced maximum in the interaction measure at $T/T_c\simeq1.09$, a strong suppression of the squared speed of sound, and a maximum in the background contribution. These correlated features characterize the substantial departure from conformal behavior in the transition region. At higher temperatures, the interaction measure decreases and the squared speed of sound approaches the conformal limit. We also examine the energy-per-excitation ratio $E/n_g$, which has a minimum of approximately $964~\mathrm{MeV}$ at $T/T_c\simeq1.21$. This ratio provides a measure of the excitation scale within the quasiparticle description. Overall, our results show how lattice thermodynamics can be mapped onto an effective gluonic excitation spectrum while maintaining thermodynamic consistency.

hep-ph.title: What Does Precision Spectroscopy Actually Constrain about X17 Couplings?
hep-ph.author: Raoul Serao, Antonio Capolupo
hep-ph.abstract: Can precision spectroscopy disentangle the individual couplings of the X17 boson? Within a leading one-body model, we combine electronic and muonic spectroscopy of hydrogen, deuterium and helium with lepton magnetic moments. We show that hydrogen-deuterium comparisons can lose neutron sensitivity through cancellations, while the combined observables restore generic local identifiability without guaranteeing finite individual bounds. The unrestricted fit admits formally unbounded nucleon-coupling directions, some of which violate the assumptions underlying the physical model. Finite-coupling tests nevertheless reveal statistically compatible solutions, with bounds dependent on nuclear responses and physical assumptions. Our results establish what precision measurements genuinely constrain and what additional information is required to extract meaningful limits on X17 couplings.

hep-ph.title: Probing Lorentz Symmetry Violation via Hadroproduction in Electroweak Pair Annihilation
hep-ph.author: S. Mohammad Moosavi Nejad, Vahid Ekraminasab
hep-ph.abstract: The violation of Lorentz symmetry is anticipated in some theories beyond the Standard Model so various processes have been studied to search for the effects of Lorentz symmetry violation (LSV). High energy collision experiments provide a suitable environment where Lorentz symmetry breaking can be examined. In this work, we study the effect of Lorentz-violating terms on the hadron production process from pair annihilation, including a vectorial nonminimal coupling between the fermions and gauge fields in the Electroweak sector. To be specific, we study the effect of CPT-odd nonminimal Lorentz symmetry violating couplings on the production of bottom flavored mesons through pair annihilation in the Electroweak theory, i.e., $e^+e^-\to q\bar{q}\to B+Jets$. Considering the available data and the analytical result for the tree-level cross section $\sigma^{LO}(e^+e^-\to B+Jets)$ in the presence of LSV terms, we determine an upper bound on the purely time-like background 4-vector as strict as $\le 10^{-3} GeV^{-1}$, in agreement with previous works on similar Lorentz violating couplings.

hep-ph.title: A Duality Model in Which Dual QCD Becomes Hydrodynamics
hep-ph.author: Noriaki Aibara, So Katagiri, Yoshiki Matsuoka, Kazuya Mitsutani, Akio Sugamoto
hep-ph.abstract: Revisiting a duality model in which dual QCD becomes hydrodynamics, or the dual gluon is a fluid, allows us to understand some of the mysteries of QCD, such as the behavior of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) as a perfect fluid and gluon saturation in the structure function at high energies. This old-fashioned duality converts the gluon action into hydrodynamics described by the 2-form stream function $W^a_{\mu\nu}$ with eight colors. All interactions then become current--current interactions of the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio type. The resulting theory admits a strong-coupling expansion about the fluid. This can provide a third method to supplement perturbative QCD and lattice QCD.

hep-ph.title: Quantum field theory treatment of the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos with diagonal magnetic moments
hep-ph.author: Maxim Dvornikov(IZMIRAN)
hep-ph.abstract: We apply the quantum field theory (QFT) approach to describe the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos. The magnetic moments matrix of these neutrinos is taken to be diagonal in the mass basis. Neutrino mass eigenstates are considered to be virtual particles in the QFT approach. The neutrino contribution to the matrix element of the overall process, which includes the emission, the propagation and the detection of neutrinos, is contained in the propagators of massive neutrinos. Using the recently derived propagator of a massive neutrino, which exactly accounts for the magnetic moment interaction, we derive the transition probability of the process $\nu_{e\mathrm{L}}\to\nu_{\mu\mathrm{L}}$ under the influence of a magnetic field. The result is compared with the prediction of the standard quantum mechanical (QM) approach. We briefly discuss the possibility to derive the QFT corrections to the QM expressions.

hep-ph.title: Heavy quarkonium spin transport in a hot medium
hep-ph.author: Nora Brambilla, Shuo Fang, Tom Magorsch, Panayiotis Panayiotou
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the in-medium spin transport of heavy quarkonium using an open-quantum-system approach based on potential nonrelativistic QCD. We express the heavy quarkonium dilepton decay angular distribution in terms of late-time quarkonium spin-dependent distribution functions. Working in the quantum-optical regime, where the inverse quarkonium size is much larger than the binding energy and the binding energy is comparable to or larger than the medium temperature $T$, we derive a spin-dependent quantum master equation incorporating both dissociation and regeneration, followed by the corresponding projected semiclassical Boltzmann equations. At leading order in the coupling, we retain the recoil corrections of relative order $T/M$ that contribute to the leading spin-dependent collision kernel. Here $M$ denotes the heavy-quark mass. At zeroth order in fluid gradients, we show that the relative motion between quarkonium and the medium supplies the leading anisotropy, while spin-chromomagnetic and spin-orbit interactions both contribute to the leading nonzero spin-alignment kernel. As an exploratory phenomenological application, we also estimate the medium-induced polarization parameter $\lambda_{\theta}$ of bottomonium $\Upsilon(1\text{S})$ using a simplified rate equation with background density matrices obtained from the Lindblad equation using QTraj. Within this simplified treatment, the resulting medium-induced polarization is found to be very small while a naive rescaling for charmonium can qualitatively describe the polarization of charmonium.

hep-ph.title: Light (anti)nuclei production via coalescence in electron-proton collisions: from HERA to EIC
hep-ph.author: Niccolò Ciavarelli, Francesco Noferini, Francesca Bellini
hep-ph.abstract: Light (anti)nuclei production provides a sensitive probe of the particle-emitting source and of the coalescence mechanism in high-energy collisions. In this work, a coalescence model implemented as an afterburner to PYTHIA 8 is validated against pp data from ALICE and ep data from ZEUS. The validated framework is then applied to ep collisions at EIC energies to predict deuteron and antideuteron production within the ePIC acceptance. The results indicate sizeable yields and a clear matter-antimatter asymmetry in the proton-going direction, making this measurement a promising observable for studying coalescence and proton structure at the EIC.

hep-ph.title: Earthquake Forecast via Neutrino Tomography at the DUNE Baseline
hep-ph.author: Bipin Singh Koranga, Samrat Vashisht, Vivek Kumar Nautiyal
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of accelerator-based neutrino oscillations to localized electron-density enhancements associated with seismic fault zones along the Fermilab SURF baseline of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE). Motivated by the reactor antineutrino proposal of Wang, Chen, and Li, we model the anomaly as a uniform-density slab embedded in the surrounding crust and calculate exact three flavour oscillation probabilities using layer by layer evolution. Our results show that localized density enhancements can produce measurable variations in muon-to-electron appearance probabilities for both neutrinos and antineutrinos, with potentially significant relative effects. The predicted variations exhibit weak dependence on the leptonic CP violating phase, suggesting that time-differential measurements may help reduce uncertainties associated with the unknown CP phase. However, the event statistics required for a statistically significant detection substantially exceed those expected during a short-duration precursor interval. Consequently, detecting sufficiently persistent density anomalies may be possible under favourable conditions, whereas short-term earthquake forecasting is not feasible with the nominal DUNE configuration. Our findings establish a theoretical framework for exploring localized Earth-density perturbations through long-baseline neutrino oscillations.

hep-ph.title: Born spreading with consistent shower starting scales in MC@NLO and FxFx merging
hep-ph.author: Rikkert Frederix, Paolo Torrielli
hep-ph.abstract: Negative weights are a major cost in NLO event generation matched to parton showers at the LHC, as they increase the number of events needed for a given statistical precision. Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative-weight $\mathbb S$ events in MC@NLO by redistributing the Born contribution over the radiation variables. It introduces no bias only if everything that is passed to the parton shower together with $\mathbb S$ events depends on Born-level quantities alone. We show that the same condition is needed for the MC counterterms to reproduce the first shower emission, independently of how the radiation phase space is integrated. In MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, the $\mathbb S$-event starting scales did not fully satisfy this condition, which so far prevented the public release of Born spreading. We present a new and consistent construction of the starting scales for ordinary MC@NLO, FxFx merging and MC@NLO-$\Delta$, with which Born spreading is now publicly available, including for merged samples. We also study modified formulations of the MC counterterms, and FxFx-merged $W$+jets production with up to two jets at NLO, for which Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative weights after merging without affecting the predictions, and the event samples are generated six times faster than with the former implementation.

hep-ph.title: Ground-State Heavy-Baryon Mass Spectrum in the Relativistic Independent Quark Model
hep-ph.author: Divyajyoti Pandey, Kalpalata Dash, Sanjay Kumar Swain
hep-ph.abstract: We extend our work to compute the ground-state baryon mass spectrum containing charm and bottom quarks in the relativistic independent quark (RIQ) model with an average flavor--independent confining potential in equally mixed scalar--vector harmonic form. Each quark moves as a Dirac particle inside the potential. The resulting core mass is then corrected perturbatively, accounting for the pion self-energy, pion exchange, and pairwise color--electric and color--magnetic one-gluon exchange. Six input parameters common to every baryon: the potential parameters (confinement strength, the potential offset) and the $u(=d)$, $s$, $c$, and $b$ constituent quark masses are optimized using a few experimentally measured baryon states. The model then uses these optimized parameters to predict the mass spectra of doubly heavy, mixed-$bc$, and triply heavy baryons. We compare our predictions with lattice QCD, relativistic quark model results, and available experimental measurements. Our results are consistent with these model predictions and experimental results.

hep-ph.title: Cross-Moment Consistency and the Fifth Adler Coefficient in Hadronic Tau Decays
hep-ph.author: Gauhar Abbas, Debabina Biswas, Pratham Dadhich, Vartika Singh
hep-ph.abstract: The unknown coefficient $c_{5,1}$ controls the first omitted fifth-order term in fixed-order analyses of inclusive hadronic $\tau$ decays. We determine what the four known Adler coefficients can actually test. For any normalized polynomial weight, the fixed-order Adler-to-moment map is triangular with unit diagonal. Hence one common Adler-coefficient error reaches every moment with the same absolute size, and a multi-weight relative test reduces to one absolute tolerance. For three representative weights, a ten-percent test resolves $c_{5,1}$ only to about $\pm24$; the closest contour-improved test is weaker by more than an order of magnitude. Moreover, any continuation that preserves the observed sign of the direct Padé/Shanks defects gives $c_{5,1}\geq378.03$, so values near $280$ require additional structure. A calibration-and-falsification protocol applied to a simplified Beneke--Jamin-type pure-power ansatz gives the conditional estimate $c_{5,1}=248\pm30\,(\mathrm{struct})\pm74\,(\mathrm{method})=248\pm80$. At the physical order its central value coincides algebraically with the exact four-parameter fit; the protocol adds a falsifiable admissibility test and a method uncertainty, not new coefficient information. We also clarify that the often-quoted Beneke--Jamin value $283$ is a linear extrapolation of total-width FOPT te

hep-ph.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
hep-ph.author: Runze Chi, Meng Zeng, Tao Xiang, Yi-Zhuang You, Bertrand I. Halperin, Juven Wang
hep-ph.abstract: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.

hep-ph.title: A Note On Lattice Definition of Gauge Theories With Chiral Fermions
hep-ph.author: Edward Witten
hep-ph.abstract: Because of the fermion doubling problem, it has been a longstanding challenge to describe a lattice algorithm for studying four-dimensional gauge theories coupled to chiral fermions. Recently, an algorithm to do so has been described by Craig, extending partial results in the previous literature. Here we describe a variant of this algorithm, based on interpolating a lattice gauge field over the continuum (as in Craig's work) and coupling the interpolated gauge field to continuum chiral fermions. The same variant was also proposed recently by Hsu. In any dimension and for any anomaly-free representation, this approach can be implemented on a computer in principle, but not in practice by Monte Carlo methods because the chiral fermion path integral is not positive.

hep-ph.title: The Search for the Top Quark
hep-ph.author: Paul D. Grannis
hep-ph.abstract: The discovery of the top quark in 1995 completed the roster of the matter particles, quarks and leptons, expected in the Standard Model and in many of its suggested extensions. However, the top quark does not conform to the pattern set by its sister quarks and has come to be a critical component of the ongoing searches for physics beyond the prevailing paradigm. (Prepared for the Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, Nov. 2025.)

hep-ph.title: Dynamics of self-gravitating halos with decaying dark matter
hep-ph.author: Anna Bencke, Marc Kamionkowski, Annika H. G. Peter, Juniper Morales
hep-ph.abstract: We study the evolution of self-gravitating spherical dark matter halos composed of dark matter particles that decay to a slightly less massive particle and a massless particle. The small kick velocity imparted to the daughter particle upon decay heats the halo. If the kick velocity is small compared with the characteristic velocity, the halo remains bound but puffs out. We also consider, for the first time, decaying halos with anisotropic initial conditions and find non-negligible effects on the resulting density profile. To simulate the halo evolution, we utilize the recently developed \texttt{NSphere} code across a broad range of decay times and kick velocities. We train an emulator to provide a mapping between the decay parameters and the relaxed density profile. We discuss how the resulting halo-scale signatures complement existing cosmological constraints on decaying dark matter and can be tested by upcoming surveys.

hep-ph.title: Satisfying Freed--Witten quantization on smooth divisors in Calabi--Yau orientifolds
hep-ph.author: Mudit Jain
hep-ph.abstract: Freed--Witten quantization conditions on several divisors wrapped by D-branes must be satisfied with one bulk $B$-field. On a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ with a holomorphic O3/O7 involution $\sigma$, we show that the common background $B_{2,+}^{\star}=\tfrac12[R]$, where $R$ is the total O7 divisor, permits Freed--Witten period quantization on the full two-cycle lattice of \emph{every smooth connected divisor}, modulo torsion. The worldvolume fluxes are chosen individually and obey the orientifold relation between each divisor and its image. The central step concerns setwise invariant divisors $D$: we prove that the bulk Freed--Witten class $\eta_D^\star=\tfrac12([R]+[D])|_D$ has integer periods on every $\sigma$-even integral two-cycle class, including inherited and autochthonous classes. Its periods on purely $\sigma$-odd classes vanish, so any remaining non-integer periods occur only on classes that are neither $\sigma$-even nor $\sigma$-odd. We show how to choose $\sigma$-odd worldvolume fluxes on these invariant divisors that make all periods integral. For exchanged divisor pairs, quantizing the flux on one member automatically quantizes its orientifold image. On invariant divisors with $h^{2,0}_-(D)=0$, the constructed flux is of type $(1,1)$ and admits a primitive representative; this includes every smooth rigid invariant divisor. We also study zero worldvolume flux on invariant divisors. For $h^{1,1}_-(X)\leq1$, we construct common bulk backgrounds satisfying every inherited intersection period on all such divisors. A binary compatibility test determines whether a common shift exists for larger $h^{1,1}_-(X)$. Non-inherited period tests then determine whether the resulting backgrounds allow zero flux on the full worldvolume lattices.

hep-ph.title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
hep-ph.author: João Barata
hep-ph.abstract: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

hep-ph.title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
hep-ph.author: V. P. Nair, Raju Venugopalan
hep-ph.abstract: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg \Lambda_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/\alpha_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $\alpha_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $\omega\leq \alpha_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

hep-ph.title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
hep-ph.author: Sabir Ramazanov, Zhen-Min Zeng
hep-ph.abstract: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The spectral shape of gravitational waves predicted in this scenario is markedly different compared to the case of domain walls remaining sub-dominant all the way till annihilation. These gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.

hep-ph.title: Gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rotating background: An eigenfunction approach
hep-ph.author: Benjamín García-Contreras, Luis A. Hernández, R. Zamora
hep-ph.abstract: We construct the free gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rigidly rotating cylindrical coordinates using an eigenfunction approach within the Feynman gauge. Starting from the quadratic gauge-fixed QCD action, we derive the corresponding kinetic operators and obtain their spectral representations. For the gluon field, a circular polarization basis diagonalizes the vector wave operator, leading to polarization-dependent shifts in the orders of the radial Bessel functions. In the absence of radial boundaries, we explicitly recover the standard Minkowski propagator in inertial Cartesian coordinates, showing that the off-diagonal tensor components in the cylindrical basis have a geometrical origin. We then extend the construction to a finite-radius cylinder satisfying the causality condition $|\Omega|R<1$, imposing relative boundary conditions on the gluon field and Dirichlet conditions on the ghosts. The resulting discrete transverse spectra involve both Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues for the gluon modes, from which we obtain explicit spectral representations of the propagators. Our results provide a consistent framework for perturbative QCD calculations in rotating geometries, retaining the angular-momentum, polarization, and boundary effects relevant to future studies of correlation functions and radiative corrections.

hep-ph.title: A search for sterile neutrinos at ultrahigh energies at the Pierre Auger Observatory
hep-ph.author: ThePierre Auger Collaboration:A. Abdul Halim, P. Abreu, M. Aglietta, M. Ahmed, I. Allekotte, K. Almeida Cheminant, R. Aloisio, J. Alvarez-Muñiz, A. Ambrosone, J. Ammerman Yebra, L. Borodai, J. Brack, P.G. Brichetto Orquera, S. Buitink, A. Bwembya, T.R. Caba Pineda, K.S. Caballero-Mora, S. Cabana-Freire, L. Caccianiga, J. Caraça-Valente, R. Caruso, A. Castellina, F. Catalani, G. Cataldi, L. Cazon, M. Cerda, B. Čermáková, A. Cermenati, K. Cerny, J.A. Chinellato, J. Chudoba, L. Chytka, R.W. Clay, A.C. Cobos Cerutti, R. Colalillo, R. Conceição, G. Consolati, M. Conte, F. Convenga, D. Correia dos Santos, P.J. Costa, C.E. Covault, M. Cristinziani, C.S. Cruz Sanchez, S. Dasso, K. Daumiller, B.R. Dawson, R.M. de Almeida, E.-T. de Boone, B. de Errico, J. de Jesús, S.J. de Jong, J.R.T. de Mello Neto, I. De Mitri, D. de Oliveira Franco, F. de Palma, V. de Souza, E. De Vito, A. Del Popolo, O. Deligny, N. Denner, K. Denner Syrokvas, L. Deval, A. di Matteo, C. Dobrigkeit, J.C. D'Olivo, L.M. Domingues Mendes, T. Dominguez, Y. Dominguez Ballesteros
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of the Pierre Auger Observatory to sterile neutrinos with masses in the MeV-to-100 MeV range. To this end, we consider a minimal $3+1$ framework in which a single sterile state mixes mainly with the $\nu_\tau$ flavor through an active--sterile mixing angle $\theta_N$ to produce a mass eigenstate $N_1$. At ultrahigh energies, $N_1$ neutrinos can traverse substantial chord lengths through the Earth and interact through their active component, producing $\tau$ leptons that may emerge near the surface and decay in the atmosphere, thereby generating detectable air showers. We compute the corresponding exposures with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of neutrino propagation, interactions, $\tau$ energy losses and decay, and derive upper limits at $90\%$ confidence level on an isotropic diffuse flux of $N_1$ neutrinos. For an $E^{-2}$ spectrum, we obtain $E^2\Phi_N\leq 2\times10^{-9}\sin^{-2}\theta_N\,\mathrm{GeV\,cm^{-2}\,sr^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$ over $0.3$--$200$ EeV for $\sin^2\theta_N\lesssim10^{-1}$. We further consider $N_1$ neutrinos arising from the decay of a superheavy dark-matter particle. For a benchmark dark-matter mass of $10^{13}$ GeV, we derive constraints on the active--sterile mixing angle and dark-matter lifetime for sterile-neutrino masses of $10$ and $100$ MeV. These results illustrate the potential of the Observatory to probe long-lived weakly interacting particles.

hep-ph.title: Primordial Black Holes and Induced Gravitational Waves from Inflation with History-Dependent Effective Dissipation
hep-ph.author: Narges Rashidi
hep-ph.abstract: We study inflation with an exponential factor multiplying the scalar Lagrangian and depending on the accumulated expansion history through a field-dependent coupling. Variation of the complete action on a finite interval yields an adjoint response with a final-time boundary condition. We derive the background and coupled scalar perturbation equations and examine five benchmarks for an exponential plateau potential and a smooth single-window coupling. The kinetic, direct-coupling and adjoint contributions nearly cancel, producing transient positive minima of the first Hubble slow-roll parameter, $\epsilon_1$, without a comparable reduction in field velocity. The scalar spectra, normalized to the cosmic microwave background (CMB) pivot amplitude, develop localized peaks with amplitudes $0.033$--$0.098$. Under Gaussian statistics and the adopted radiation-era collapse prescription, the the primordial black hole (PBH) abundance peaks span masses from $4.52\times10^{-13}$ to $34.05\,M_\odot$. The lightest-mass benchmark reaches $f_{\rm PBH}\simeq0.99$, allowing nearly all dark matter within the monochromatic approximation. The accompanying scalar-induced gravitational-wave spectra span peak frequencies from $6.78\times10^{-10}$ to $5.92\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{Hz}$, with selected benchmarks lying within the projected sensitivities of future detectors.

hep-ph.title: Planting neutrino SE-EdS: A < 3% accurate clustering approximation for neutrinos and other hot dark matter
hep-ph.author: Amol Upadhye, Yvonne Y. Y. Wong
hep-ph.abstract:
The age of the cosmic neutrino is upon us. Aside from their fundamental importance to particle physics and the recent tensions in their mass scale $M_
u = \sum m_
u$, neutrinos' degeneracies with other cosmological parameters in analyses of scale-dependent cosmic clustering will significantly affect the estimates of these parameters, making accurate, inexpensive, easily-implemented approximations essential tools for theoretical cosmology. We present a new linear approximation, SE-EdS, applicable to non-relativistic neutrinos and other hot dark matter, which is exact in the linear Einstein-de Sitter case, and < 3% accurate for a broad range of flat and non-flat cosmologies characterized by parameters $0.2 \leq \Omega_{m,0} \leq 1$, $0 \leq \Omega_{
u,0} \leq 0.018$, $-0.1 \leq \Omega_{K,0} \leq 0.1$, and $w_0 \leq -0.6$, at all length scales. This broad coverage in $\Omega_{m,0}$ makes SE-EdS ideal for N-body simulations, whose redshift range $z \lesssim 100$ demands accuracy for time-dependent $\Omega_m$ between unity and the preferred late-time values $\sim 0.3$. SE-EdS may be used to paint neutrinos into simulations in Fourier space, where its < 3% error and neutrinos' $\leq$ 3% matter fraction guarantees < 0.1% errors in the total matter density contrast, thereby including neutrino effects upon clustering at negligible computational cost. We quantify the approximation's accuracy; extend it to a broad range of cosmologies; and explore its correspondence with higher-order corrections to existing linear response schemes. A simple implementation is available online atthis https URL.

hep-ph.title: Inflationary attractors in metric-affine gravity
hep-ph.author: Ilaria Andrei, Christian Dioguardi
hep-ph.abstract: We study single-field slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity (MAG). We consider the most general action up to operators linear in curvature and quadratic in the distortion, without propagating torsion and non-metricity. We first impose projective invariance and promote every coefficient to a function of the scalar field. After integrating out the non-dynamical distortion, the net contribution is a correction $k(\phi)$ to the scalar kinetic term. We then consider the class of $\xi$-attractors for which the non-minimal couplings and the scalar potential are fixed by a single function $f(\phi)$. It is well-known that in the metric formulation the strong-coupling regime is universally the Starobinsky attractor. In the Palatini framework, instead, this attractor is lost and the predictions become model-dependent. Here, we show that the MAG framework restores universality: in the strong coupling limit with finite ratios of the distortion couplings to $\xi$ we have an $\alpha$-attractor, $n_s=1-2/N_*$ and $r=12\alpha/N_*^2$, with $\alpha=1+\zeta/(6\xi)$. The ratio $\zeta/\xi$ encodes the distortion contribution. Starobinsky and Palatini inflation are recovered as specific limits. Through a numerical parameter scan we show that almost all the healthy points lie on one of the two attractors : either Nieh-Yan-like inflation (studied in a previous work and extended here) or the new MAG $\alpha$-attractor found here.
